title: Developer tools and the eval bench
bridge: A poe task is like an npm script with named arguments and help text. A Harbor task is like a Playwright spec folder for an agent. It holds an instruction, an environment and a test script that decides pass or fail. Except: poe can run a Python function, not only a shell string. And the Harbor test judges a whole agent run inside a container and writes a number, the reward, to a file.
intro: Two kinds of tooling make agents useful in fcp. Developer tools give one command that means the same thing in the editor, in the sandbox and in CI. They are poe verify, poe doctor and a one-page failure report. The eval bench runs the real Nova harness on real past tickets and scores it. This lesson covers both, because both live in Python and both are things you will add to.

p: poethepoet (poe) is npm scripts for a uv project. Tasks live in the [tool.poe.tasks] table of pyproject.toml. fcp's root pyproject already has cloud-up, cloud-migrate, backend-integration-tests, frontend-test and health, and .claude/settings.json allows Bash(poe *) for agents.
A cmd task is a shell command string with an optional cwd and help. A script task names a Python function by import path, with typed arguments that become flags.

uv run poe <task> runs it inside .venv. uvx --from poethepoet poe <task> runs it without installing anything, which is what CI and the sandbox image use. Extra arguments after the task name go to the command.
sections.because: Every G7 command an agent or a person runs is a poe task, so the table is the menu of the repo.

notes.text: A cmd task. cwd runs it in the cloud project; help shows in uv run poe with no arguments. The fixed seed makes the order reproducible.
A comment in TOML starts with #. The ticket keeps the open question (testmon with -n) right next to the task.
The affected variant: same layer, --testmon instead of -n auto. poe api-test-affected -k vocab passes -k through.

sections.h: poe verify: one command, three callers
p: G7-14 adds a script task, verify, that lints the changed Python files and runs the affected tests for each area that changed. Three callers run the same command.
A Claude Code Stop hook in fcp's .claude/settings.json is one. Nova's harness is another (it loads the project settings, so the same hook runs). CI with --all is the third.
A Stop hook is a command Claude Code runs when the agent says it is done. Exit 2 with a message on stderr sends the agent back to work with that message; exit 0 lets it stop.

The hook script checks stop_hook_active in its input. When it is already inside a stop, it lets the session end, so it never loops. This is feedback, not a cage: verify tells the agent what is red, and the agent keeps working until it is green.
sections.because: When the editor, the agent and CI run the same command, green means the same thing everywhere. Agents stop guessing which checks to run.

notes.text: The task is verify = { script = "scripts.poe_verify:main(all_files=all)", args = [{ name = "all", type = "boolean" }] }. The flag --all becomes this argument.
The merge base again (p10-5): changed means changed since main, plus untracked files on the next line.
Lint only the changed files, with the same pre-commit hooks CI runs (black, isort, flake8).
FULL_RUN is migrations/, fixtures/ and tests_api/conftest.py: the files testmon cannot see (p10-2), so the whole layer runs.
One line per step at the end, so the summary fits in an agent's context.
On failure, point at the one-page report instead of printing the log again.

sections.h: poe doctor: check a machine, fix only what is safe
p: G7-22 adds doctor, a list of checks with a fix per check. It checks node and npm versions from frontend/package.json engines, Python 3.13 through uv, and uv sync --check for the cloud venv. It checks Docker memory of at least 16 GiB, the rhino-net Docker network and poe itself. It also checks the git hooks problem: husky sets core.hooksPath, so the Python pre-commit hooks never run on commit.
--fix runs only safe local commands (uv python install, make sync-deps, docker network create) and prints them. It never touches credentials, ~/.aws or Docker volumes.

--json prints one JSON object per check, one per line, for machines. G7-25 runs poe doctor --json inside the nightly sandbox image build and fails the build when a check fails. So a broken fresh setup never becomes the image Nova runs on.
sections.because: Setup problems cost about 86 hours per developer per year. An agent in a fresh VM hits the same problems with less patience.

code.file: scripts/poe_doctor.py (G7-22, the checks table and main)

notes.text: A table of tuples. Adding a check is adding a row; the loop below does not change.
lambda: a one-expression anonymous function, evaluated later by the loop. _run returns stdout or None when the command is missing or fails.
uv sync --check exits non-zero when .venv does not match uv.lock; the fix is safe, so --fix may run it.
Docker's memory from docker info, compared in bytes. Not safe to fix: a person changes Docker's settings.
The guard: only a failing check whose fix is marked safe runs under --fix.
JSON lines for machines (the image build), aligned text for people.

sections.h: Test output an agent can read
p: A 3,000-line log fills an agent's context. G7-12 adds a pytest plugin that writes reports/failures.md after the run. For each failing test it gives the node id, file and line, and the first error line.
Then the last 40 lines of the traceback and an exact rerun command with the seed. It caps at 20 failures and points at reports/junit.xml for the rest. Under xdist only the controller writes it.

JUnit XML is the old, boring, universal test report format: one <testcase> per test with its status and message. CI tools, the nightly history in G7-24 and the flaky-test fixer all read it. --junitxml=reports/junit.xml makes pytest write it.
The seed comes from pytest-randomly. With --randomly-seed=1009 the tests run in the same shuffled order every time, and Faker and factory_boy are reseeded. So a failure reproduces.
sections.because: An agent fixes its own mistakes only when the failure is short, complete and comes with the command to reproduce it.
sections.see:

sections.h: The eval bench: a Harbor task
p: ai-agents/evals is a small uv project inside the TypeScript repo, because Harbor, the bench runner, is Python. CI runs it as its own job. First uv sync --frozen --project evals, then black, isort and flake8 at 120 columns, then uv run --project evals pytest. TICKET-BENCH (G4-02, G4-03, G4-25) and ROUTINE-BENCH (G5-10) live there.

A Harbor task is a folder. instruction.md is what the agent reads (the ticket text). task.toml holds the configuration and metadata. environment/ describes the container (a Dockerfile, or a prebuilt image named in task.toml).

solution/solve.sh applies the real fix; only Harbor's oracle agent uses it, to prove the task is solvable. tests/test.sh runs after the agent and must write a number to /logs/verifier/reward.txt: 1 for pass, 0 for fail. tests/hidden/ holds the PR's real test files at their real paths. They are copied in only at grading time, so the agent never sees them.

The task.toml field names depend on the Harbor version pinned in evals/pyproject.toml. The ticket sketch starts with version = "1.0"; the current Harbor docs show schema_version and a [task] table with a name. Check the docs for the pinned version before you copy the sketch.
sections.because: The bench has to test the same Nova that runs real tickets. The task format tells Harbor how to build that run.

code.file: tasks/fe-bug-1234/task.toml (G4-03, in the restricted golden-set repo)
code.text:
version = "1.0"

[metadata]
kind = "fe_bug"                 # fe_bug | be_bug | add_tests | small_feature | dependency_bump
multi_file = false
source_repo = "RhinoHealth/fcp"
source_pr = 1234
jira = "RH-1234"
base_sha = "<parent of the squash commit on main>"
hidden_tests = ["frontend/test/unit/<file>.test.tsx"]
smoke = false                   # true for the 15 tasks in the smoke set
curated_by = "<BE or FE engineer>"

[agent]
# A far-away eval backstop only, to free a stuck eval VM. Nova itself has no time limit:
# minutes per task are measured and reported, and a timeout is reported as "stuck", not as a slow pass.
timeout_sec = 21600.0

[verifier]
timeout_sec = 3600.0

[environment]
cpus = 8
memory_mb = 32768

notes.text: metadata is free-form: anything the scorer needs later. kind splits the scores; multi_file flags the 5 big cases.
The commit the container is reset to: the parent of the squash commit, so the fix is not there yet.
The real tests from the merged PR, at their real paths. They come in at grading time; the agent never sees them.
Six hours, to free a stuck eval VM, and a timeout counts as stuck in the report. It is not a limit on Nova: no maxTurns, no budget, nothing cuts a run.
How long the hidden tests may take. One hour covers a frontend e2e set.
A full-size container, like the full VM: FCP Lab and browsers fit.

callout.text: Candidates and tasks go to the restricted golden-set repo, never to ai-agents or rnd-kb, so the brain never indexes the answers. Ticket text comes from a read-only Jira token; attachments are never downloaded.

sections.h: The adapter starts the real harness
p: Harbor runs an agent through an adapter, a Python class that knows how to start the agent inside the task container. G4-03's nova_agent.py starts the TypeScript harness CLI, nova-worker run <task.json>, on the base commit with the instruction. The task image carries Node 24 and the harness tarball from release-harness.yml (one bundled file, nothing to install) next to fcp's toolchain. So the bench runs exactly the harness that runs real tickets.
Bench mode strips the people out. The plan is auto-approved, and a question gets "no answer, use your judgement". There is no Jira, Slack or PR; the result is the working tree.

Answer leaks are stopped on two sides. The checkout is reset to base_sha with git mirror refs dropped. And in bench mode the broker refuses to read the source PR and anything merged after base. So the similar-past-PRs helper cannot find the answer.

Trials need a VM each. G4-25 adds an evalRun workflow in the orchestrator on its own eval queue with fixed slots. So bench runs never take Nova's VMs, and only the orchestrator starts runs. Where do trials run: a fresh full VM per trial on the same AMI, or Harbor's docker environment inside one wide VM? That decision is written into evals/ticket_bench/README.md.

sections.h: Scoring: pass@1, pass^3, and numbers that are never limits
p: Each task runs three times. pass@1 is the mean success rate over trials. pass^3 is the chance that all three trials of a task pass, which measures consistency.

A task that passes once in three has pass^3 of zero. Cost per task comes from the gateway's run tag (bench:<task>:<try>), minutes from Harbor's trial timings. The report splits by kind, with the 5 big cases on their own.
The 15-task smoke set runs on every ai-agents PR that touches the harness, prompts, skills or the image, one try per task. With 15 tasks, one task is about 6.7 points.
So a drop of one task means run again, and two or more fail the check. The full 40 run monthly on a Temporal schedule. Cost and minutes are measured to learn; they are never used as limits on a run.
sections.because: This is how we decide whether a harness change, a new skill or a cheaper model setting helps. So the arithmetic must be right.

notes.text: comb(n, k) counts combinations. With 3 tries and 2 wins, comb(2,3) is 0, so pass^3 is 0; with 3 wins it is 1.
sum of booleans: True counts as 1. reward comes from reward.txt.
Per task: pass@1 is wins over tries; pass^3 uses the function above. Cost is a mean, minutes a median, both reported, never enforced.

quiz.q: Nova's Stop hook runs poe verify, which fails. What happens next?

options.text: The run is cancelled and the ticket goes back to the requester.
options.why: Nothing cancels a run; the hook is feedback, not a cage.

options.text: The hook exits 2 with the summary and the failures.md path on stderr, and the agent keeps working on the red steps.
options.why: Exit 2 sends the agent back with the message; stop_hook_active prevents an endless loop.

options.text: The failure is logged and the agent is allowed to stop.
options.why: That is what happens only when stop_hook_active is already true, to avoid a loop.

quiz.q: Why is the [agent] timeout_sec in a TICKET-BENCH task.toml not a violation of the no-limits rule?

options.text: Because six hours is long enough for any ticket.
options.why: Length is not the argument; what the number is used for is.

options.text: It exists only to free a stuck eval VM. A timeout is reported as stuck, never counted as a result or used to stop a real Nova run.
options.why: The ticket says so in the comment, and Nova's own harness has no maxTurns, budget or time limit.
Harbor's docs say the agent timeout defaults to no timeout.

quiz.q: A task was run 3 times: pass, fail, pass. What are pass@1 and pass^3 for it?

options.why: pass^3 asks whether all three pass; one failed, so it is 0.
2 wins out of 3 trials; comb(2, 3) is 0, so pass^3 is 0.
pass@1 is the mean success rate, 2/3, not whether any trial passed.

words.plain: An entry in [tool.poe.tasks] in pyproject.toml: a shell command or a Python function with named arguments and help text.
A command Claude Code runs when the agent wants to stop; exit 2 with a message sends the agent back to work.
A table of checks with a fix each. --fix runs only the safe local fixes, and --json prints one object per check for machines.
The universal test report file, one testcase element per test; pytest writes it with --junitxml and many tools read it.
A folder with instruction.md, task.toml, an environment, an optional solution and tests/test.sh that judges an agent run.
The number tests/test.sh writes to /logs/verifier/reward.txt: 1 for pass, 0 for fail.
The chance that k trials of a task all pass; with 3 trials it measures consistency, next to the mean pass@1.

tickets.why: poe verify is the script task, the Stop hook and the CI --all call explained here.
poe doctor is the checks table with safe fixes and JSON output shown in this lesson and its lab.
The Harbor task folder, task.toml and the Python adapter that starts nova-worker run are this lesson's bench half.
score.py's pass@1 and pass^3, the smoke set on harness PRs and the one-task noise rule come from here.

remember: One command that means the same thing everywhere (poe verify), and one report an agent can read (failures.md). A bench runs the real harness and writes a reward. Cost and minutes are measured, never limits.
